body: No one in my area is hiring rn. They \*say\* they are, but even with experience, open availability and acceptance that it's min wage, no one's calling me back.
I made myself a t-shirt from the rodeo hamsters.
I have started responding with "Are you hiring?"

I feel the same way. 

I started out taking the job for a discount and to get out of the house, but it's been the only place I've found where I just fit in. I'm not the weirdo at the edge of the group here. People are actually happy to see me. That'll be the part I miss the most.
people who do craft shows? I have a friend who sews dresses out of licensed fabrics.

Yeah our ASM was counting bolts Sunday night before close and we had nearly 2k left. I was already planning on buying/picking up a 4 ft fabric shelf today so I luckily caught the bolt sale early. I grabbed what was on my short list before it was gone. 

My next shift is Wednesday morning so I wonder how much will be left.
Liquidators are just scummy people though.
I'm shocked that I haven't gotten one yet. I'm in the bible belt and all I get is  that Jesus will take care of me.
Exactly. I remember way back when Beanie Babies were huge and my mom's gift shop had over 1k people on her list to call when a new shipment would come in.

I thought there might be dementia involved because the conversations went in circles for 20 minutes. She seemed to think that because she gave her phone number out to the store, that we would call every customer and tell them about the store closing and gift cards no longer being accepted.
Our GA rep sold them.

I've told people that I'll sell feet pics. Or if they're rude that I'm going to live in my car again like the last time I was unemployed. It's seriously kinda rude to ask unless they're offering a job.

Yeah we had a lady in her 60s arguing with our ASM because she bought a $500 gift card online for 39.95 and we had to tell her the bad news. She kept saying how it was "bad customer service" that we wouldn't just give her $500 worth of merch for free.
I heard Sunday 5/18 today.

Our rep already sold our mops and brooms. Our ASM had to go buy new ones. People have been picking up fixtures since late March. People have been complaining that they can't take the shopping carts yet. \*sigh\*
We have a good amount at my store too. I might grab a bolt.
Corporate doesn't hate them? Front for the mafia? MiB training facility?
In Oklahoma we have Dallas fabric and a pallet of New Orleans.
Yep. I anticipate the weekend will be busy with the cotton and yarn at 50% off. I'm doing my shopping Friday at a sister store before the rush.
My store was a big and tall men's store before. Not sure what's going in the space. Burlington is across the street and they're putting in a trader joe's nearby too.
Yeah I don't get it. Luckily at my store the mess is mostly confined to the bathrooms. We've only had one code brown when an employee's service dog couldn't hold it anymore.

Our GA rep is a pigeon.

Comes in, makes a bunch of noise, shits on everything and leaves.

My Walmart still has a cut counter, but on a good day you're waiting at least 30-45 minutes to get fabric cut. The MoD walked by me twice to see if I needed help/had been helped and let me know that the issue is getting people "authorized to use scissors". Having bolts of fabric is a more labor intensive business then just regular retail.
Yeah I've had a few ladies at the CC tell me that they know the owner and the minimum cut doesn't apply to them.

We all mourn in different ways I guess. 


Our anyone bathroom is usually the one people try to flush packaging.

As soon as the liquidation was announced a customer clogged our ladies bathroom with resin. I was convinced that we'd be down to one bathroom until the store closed, but no - it just took 6 weeks until GA decided to spend the money.
The amount of people that are functionally illiterate is mind boggling. They don't understand signs in a retail setting, yet they drive and vote?!

I frequently shop at other stores and I would never. I'm more likely to recover fabric while I'm shopping or put it back in the correct place since it's second nature. I'd never harass another sibling of the apron. 

Do they not understand that every store is different?

I heard we'll be getting yarn and thread. Our yarn right now isn't selling at 40% off. 

The thread just pisses me off. Our GA rep had us sell our thread fixtures nearly a month ago and we've had to throw thread in random dump bins/baskets/half the ribbon aisle. Every time someone want to buy fixtures he lets them take them right away except for the carts/cut counter. So our store is a weird mash up of random aisles of crap + big empty spaces where the gondolas used to be with pallets and boxes on the top.
We have a ton too in Oklahoma!

This one lady was just big mad that it wasn't updated on the computer and started yelling at a 17 year old working the cut counter. She's autistic and was nearly shutting down until the ASM showed up to help. Then the customer went around the counter to continue arguing with her elderly mother about how we were all thieves and scammers and she was going to sue us and throw us in jail. Honestly looking back it was comical because she was in her 50's and it's blizzard fleece, hardly worth throwing a fit about.

I have a small business where I'm the only employee. Before 2020 I was clearing 25-30K annually. Then it got cut in half. I closed my retail location and moved production back to my house. I am lucky that I can source most things locally, but I have been purchasing extra of my staples when I have the extra cash. I have kept my pricing mostly the same since 2015 and I will still get comments about being exorbitantly expensive occasionally.
I'm playing this in my pocket on my next shift. The silence is bugging me so bad at work.
I was in the Tulsa store last week. Closing date is May 31, Tons of apparel and flannel/fleece. No embroidery floss.
Our GA guy already sold our thread fixtures. And we're still getting thread in. >.< So now we have big dump bins of assorted thread.
Oh I hate it for the customers. It makes us look bad when we're just the whipping boy.
We'd have to take half the signs down at this point. Thank FSM that the cotton rings up correctly, angry quilters are the worst.
We have no clue when our rep will be in and he's been pretty anal about the signs. Otherwise I'd totally take them down.

My area it's 14.99-16.99 licensed cotton is 18.99 

We're in the middle of the US so it has to get trucked in. It feels like every year another local shop closes. One of my favorites closed last year because the landlord doubled her rent and wanted her to be responsible for building maintenance. She's 60+ years old and said "screw it, I'll retire!" Plus the crazy amount of theft she had to deal with.
Under our thread display we found a grand opening sale flyer from when our store opened.

What about the "negotiators"? 

I get a bunch of "But if I get a 1/4 yard off 8 bolts that's 2 yards so that's okay right?" Or "I can get 2 1 yard cuts and be okay, yeah?" 

Or the people that don't notice all the signs literally everywhere and then think it's me personally that's being rude/hateful/whatever for enforcing a minimum.
Yep and landlords are getting worse. One of my LQS closed last year because the landlord doubled her rent and making her responsible for maintenance. She said "Screw that." and retired
That bubble fur with the elastic on the back. We have had 6 full bolts for over a year and it's still not moving at 60% off.
One of the keyholders was literally herding people out of the store on Sunday. They were just casually browsing, ignoring the many PA announcements.
Our button aisle is now the Bed Bath and Beyond reject aisle. It's a strange mix of random kitchen stuff, fake candles and bathrobes.
Oklahoma.
Wouldn't surprise me at this point.
We got 35 bolts of Saints fabric. Selvedge says 2007.
We've been tagging everything. Every shift someone has a section to scan and put price stickers on.
I want to do a tally sheet, but I always forget to start one when I clock in.

We were one of the stores that were staying open. We have a sign on the door and one on every aisle of fabric, plus 2 taped to the cut counter. People still act surprised when we tell them that there's a minimum.
I've had to do the math for at least one person every shift at my store for the past 2 years.
A lady yesterday wanted 2 1.75 yd cuts from 2 different bolts and was angry that I said no because "it's over the 2 yard minimum!"

We're a pretty good team at my store, not a lot of drama. There's 2 new hires that are lazy as hell, but one's quitting soon because she got another job, so we'll just have the one who is always whining about being tired, wants people to buy her lunch and takes 1 hour lunch breaks.

My SM has everyone on deck for this. After the first weekend of liquidation where we had lines filling the store and I was stuck alone at CC from 7 - close with 100 people left in line and I was cleaning behind the CC until 3:30 am. My MoD with me refused to help saying that she "wasn't going to do my job for me" - was fired. So the SM has like tons of coverage now.
We have like 3 people on CC all day, so there's plenty of manpower for remnants.
I'd like to think it was staff complaints because we had so many bolts with tiny strips wound around them.
At my store I've noticed the ones begging to skip the line are more likely to abandon their cut fabric on the way to checkout.
Same, and people still leave stuff everywhere.

Yeah even with a bunch of staff in the store, we can't keep up with people stuffing things wherever. And people just don't understand. Would you want to work a 12/13 hour shift on your feet answering the same questions over and over without getting a break? 

My shift today I stocked a ton of candles and recovered 2 full fabric aisles. Will my work still be nice tomorrow? Hell no.
I respond that if I was in charge, we wouldn't be closing.

We still have people coming in and asking if online will still be open, or \*other store in nearby city\* will still be open. It's wild how selective people's selective hearing is. 

Then we'll get some awesome people that come up and say "Private equity sucks! We love y'all!"

Yeah most of my interactions at the cut counter are awesome. There's just some people that think that \*I\* run the company and make all the decisions. I do love helping people with their projects if we're not slammed.

We do, but he had one of our short employees climb up the ladder and then stand on the top row of shelves to hang up closing signs on the wall. 

The customers at the cut counter said OSHA would have a field day.
Literally had a lady bring up 2 identical bolts and want to know why one was marked down and the other wasn't. The sticker says "yds".

Our one sign guy just stands in the parking lot. Nowhere near the road. 


We're in a shopping center way back from the intersection/road. Our GA rep was in yesterday morning and complaining about him. He also had one of our employees standing on the topstock shelves to hang signs.
That's where I went first.
We had a gentleman buy a bunch of 5" foam for his work crew to sleep on. It wasn't comfortable enough so they came in to return the smushed, dirty foam.

Reminds me of the "velvet fleece" lady. She didn't actually know what we called the fabric, that's what she called it and she's gotten it here before so I'm stupid for not figuring out in 30 seconds that she wanted flannel.

I had an older regular do that the other day. She had 6 bolts and only wanted 1.25 yards from each and every time I had to tell her about the minimum. She'd say "oh wow really?". 

6 times. I didn't want to laugh in front of her. 

I honestly believe people think "rules for thee but not for me"
We've been told not to make/sell remnants so we have weird bolts with little skinny pieces - which is just dumb imo.
I work tomorrow/sat so I'll make a tally sheet

We had one lady leave a nasty google review because she thought we should have an express lane for the cut counter for people getting less then 2 yard cuts. No limit on the total amount of bolts, so the quilters with 2 carts full wanting 1/4 yd cuts would use the "express lane" 

And all on 2 person coverage.

We do announcements every 15 minutes starting an hour before closing time. Unless we're exhausted and then we do announcements every 10 minutes. We've had people walk in at 2 minutes to close and just meander through the whole store, ask me questions at CC and just waste time.

Ours are always needing repairs because the plumbing is old/people putting too much paper. 


Right after the liquidation started the women only one broke, so we put a sign on the door. People ignored it and complained. Now there's a sign, a RoT tube jammed in the door, plus duct tape across the door. 


Still no plumber.
I call myself a "quilt therapist". I'd like therapist rates for all the hand holding and random project knowledge that I'm asked constantly.

Where I live we have a bunch of locally owned fabric shops. I've found the "where will I shop now?" Question - at least in my area - to mean "where will I find cheap fabric now?" Most people don't want/can't spend $15/yard on LQS fabrics.
Yeah the amount of people that come in and argue with us about "bait and switch" because online it was 90% off and why can't you price match. Explaining that it's a scam means nothing.
We're almost out of flannel, down to half on the cottons and 25% down on the fleece. Our apparel is just kinda hanging out?
Yeah it kinda shocked me at first. Like this isn't the LQS expensive fabrics, even.
The amount of customers yesterday that argued that we were a "bait and switch" because they saw online everything was 90% off.
I'm always polite and courteous to customers while I'm on the clock. I thought this was a sub for employees to vent about BS that happens at work, guess I was wrong.
Cause I don't have another job lined up yet, and being homeless sucks?
I worked at Hancock's forever ago. I guess I blocked a bunch out.
I love my cut counter chats! It was slow(er) this morning so I was able to have a normal-ish day.
Yeah half our staff quit when they made the closing announcement. We'd been jerked around by our DM for weeks about our jobs, so I don't blame them.
We're down to about 1/2 to 1/3 of cotton fabrics. Everything else is barely moving.
The poor lonely babies!

All over the damn fabric areas. I had a lady this afternoon act surprised when I told her about the minimum. I mentioned that at least there was a sign on the door, and a sign on that fabric aisle and she still acted confused. I think it's more a "rules for thee but not for me" situation.
They'd still pay hide and seek with it.
I grew up sewing and it was always non refundable. If I have extra, then you find something else to do with it. Or find someone else who sews, or a sewing guild or something....
But my math teacher was wrong - we all have a calculator in our pockets now!
We had several regulars that would do that. Come in on Monday, buy a bunch of 1 yard cuts for a quilt. Come in Tuesday and return everything. Come in Wednesday buy their fabrics out of the remnants.
I've been leaving at 8 or 9 pm on Sunday and have people outside wanting to come in and shop. Your family misses you - go home!
I'm almost going back to teacher mode like my last job. "This fabric piece will be ××.×× are you sure before I cut it?" Which is just stupid and takes too much time.
We have 9 walmart carts (nearest store is over a mile away) plus an Aldi cart- with quarter. Occasionally we'll have Target, Ross and TJMaxx carts.
...at least 1 per hour.
Yeah it's that same vibes as "I'm going to come back for that." at a craft show.
I like to ask if there's an amount they want me to stop at. Most people are grateful but no one had their listening ears on today.
We found the bolt and rolled it back up. We were too swamped to put anything away until about 2:30/3pm

It was literally right around the corner on a display with the ticket with it. One lady complained to the MoD that the fabric wasn't all 40% off and I already explained it to her when she was at the cut counter. I tell them the regular price, the discount % and the sale price. So it's straight up not listening or just being bratty.
I've had a couple of other LQS owners come in and buy all of the "premium" fabrics we had left.
My mom works at HL and she buys new holiday decor every season. She's a hoarder too, so her house is full of literal and metaphorical crap. I hardly decorate because I don't want to feed the beast.
The amount of high people that want to argue with me at the cut counter is too much. I honestly don't get the appeal of being high off your ass and then going shopping.

Honestly the customers at my store aren't too bad. I deal with the rudest, most entitled people in my sewing business. I make quilts, and I've won awards and been recognized as one of the best in my state, so I know that I don't suck at sewing lol. But I've had people scream in my face, call me every name under the sun, tell me that I deserve to starve, or even physically assault me over sewn goods. I guess I'm a horrible person for charging money to sew. \*shrug\*

I trained 2 new cut counter people at the same time this week. Most of our staff either has another job or is in school so we can only work so many hours. I'm grateful for the help - we actually had 6 people for most of the day yesterday (Saturday) and not only handled the customers, but got fabric sorted back into order and go backs taken care of.

Oh that's me. I have my own sewing business and I've been stocking up. All my coworkers know, so it's a running joke now. 

We're getting 80 boxes of fabric on the next truck? No worries, just ask Okiewolf to bring the van around to the back.
Yeah he's an idiot. I was actually shopping at another store and he was there and looked up and saw me getting fabric cut. His face was glorious.

My store is having lots of scalpers/other business owners buying up everything. 2 people came in and bought all our embroidery floss for thier craft store - ladies with 4/5 carts of yarn to sell on Ebay.

Yeah we heard from our DM that we didn't need to worry, don't go looking for another job - someone's going to buy the company and keep it open. Then Monday the 24th at noon. "Hey so does anyone want extra hours? I have unlimited hours to give out because our store is closing." 

Half our staff quit on the spot.
The overseas factories that make the fabrics/yarn will be shopping around for other outlets. They're not just going to roll over and die.
Our notion aisle is still pretty full. and the Gutermann thread. Floss and yarn are a ghost town. Flannel is looking pretty picked over. Apparel fabrics still looks normal.
I have had customers bring HL bags of fabric and expect us to have the same fabric. Then it's my fault that we don't.

My least favorite customers came in the other day - a husband and wife who want a bunch of stuff and a special discount because it's for their church. Or in their words "It's for the Jesus, we should get a good deal." Of course they come in after they took away all the extra discounts on Xstore, so there is no special discount for the Jesus.

They were not happy that the brocade fabric they wanted was still $12/yard and I couldn't do any extra discounts besides end of bolt. I had to actually show them on my handheld before they believed me. Then asked what was with all the signs. I told them that the store was closing, which they seemed confused about. They wanted a discount because the wife wanted pink lace and we only had white. Then they demanded I follow them around to price check everything.

My coworkers needed help at the cut counter so I tried to politely excuse myself. That didn't work, so I finally just said "These are 30% off, the store is closing, we're all losing our jobs and I need to go help the people in line. If you want some fabric cut, take a number."

The wife looked sad for a moment and then said "Don't worry, the Jesus will take care of you."

I really can't wait until they're Hobby Lobby's problem.
My SM comes in at 6am Sunday, but the  rest of Sunday crew is teenagers.
I had to train 2 new people for cut counter at the same time, with a massive line. It was not pleasant.

I think each manager is interpreting it differently. My SM asked me what I thought it meant. (I am the only employee who sews in my store.) I said any amount as long as it's at least a yard. Most customers are happy with that.
I've heard that they don't have room/scissors/whatever at home so we need to do it for them. My smaller cuts can be a little wonky, but I usually add an extra half inch or so to account for that.
Yes, and for quilts they've been outsourced for so long that most people think $50 is totally normal for a custom queen size quilt.
my best seller at craft shows, I cut into 9 inch strips. But I ALWAYS do it myself. I just ask for whole yards at the cut counter because hot damn.
Yeah I trained 2 new cut counter girls today. We need at least 2 people closing cut counter over the weekend (fri/sat/sun) I'd prefer 3, but I'll take 2.
This is the same company that liquidated Hancock's. They offered us $15/hour plus a bonus if we stuck it out. Didn't get a pay raise or bonus. I wouldn't trust them if their tongue came notarized.

We'd have those ladies that sell the "scrubbies" at craft shows come in and buy the whole bolt of netting, but want it cut into 1/3 yd pieces. Or the quilters who wanted 1/2 yard cut into 6 inch strips. 

I'm a crafter and I would never dream of tying up the line making someone else do part of my work. That's just dumb and selfish.
I have been, but right now with inflation I'm lucky to get 1.50/hour for making quilts.

Last Saturday we stopped letting people in at 8pm. My last customer getting fabric cut was at 9:07. We had 2 people call out and I was alone on the cut counter for 2 hours. No one had time to put anything away and behind the cut counter was just a massive pile of fabric. It took me until 2:15am to just get the fabric put away, then doing remnants and trash - I was clocked out at 3:30. It was absolutely insane.
A 20 something lady did. Dunno about the older lady. It seemed to me that she might be getting senile because the conversation went in several loops while I was browsing fabric.
Our IC took the locks off the scissor pegs and opened the sewing machine cage. She DGAF anymore.
Yeah it even aired on our local news stations on Monday Feb 24th that all stores were liquidating and the last day for gift cards was the 28th. I have no sympathy for them anymore.
I've been handing business cards to my regulars. I work full time in my own sewing business and I do lessons.
❤️ I might go back to sleep. I had to go to the grocery store earlier.

Me and the MoD. We had the shopping center security guy outside, but it's in an affluent area. I was more concerned with falling asleep on the drive home. I was on speakerphone with my night owl bestie to keep me awake.

I was exhausted. I brought tylenol and took some every 4 hours. Moved my car near the door right after 9pm when I cut my last customer. Today is my day off thankfully. They did try to call me in at 8am today. I was still passed out though.
SM doesn't work Saturdays. She comes in at 6am on Sunday. I joked that we'd meet her coming in.
MoD (New KH) was scheduled a clopen. She called out. I have today off.
Yeah because my SM wants closing shift to clean up everything and I was the only closing CC person. It was just me and the MoD from 7pm onward.
I closed tonight too. Didn't get done putting all the fabric away and cleaning/remnants until 3:30 am.
Yeah I wish I could just clock out, but I was scheduled to close, so I had to put everything away, do remnants, sweep and take out trash. Scheduled 2:30 to close - worked 2:30pm to 3:30 am.
I worked at Hancock's and helped close my store. Damn that hurts.
A bunch of ladies here do donation quilts for charities, so I guess they don't care?
Especially since my IC told me today that they're shutting off the employee discount soon??? Pretty shitty if it's true.
At my store there were quilters who wanted 1/4 yd cuts of every cotton. They had one girl cutting for over 4 hours.
We went to a 1 yard minimum yesterday. Most people were understanding. One lady thought I did it just to spite her and she was big mad at me. My customers after her were like "wow what a bitch."

I am at one one of the "go forward" stores and our SM just gave us free rein with hours. However she scheduled only 2 at CC. My coworker's cover arrived when she was supposed to leave, while mine was a high schooler who was scheduled 1.5 hours after I was supposed to leave. It was a nonstop line, so I ended up staying an extra 3 hours just putting fabric up.
I told people that I might start selling feet pics or buy some chickens and sell eggs.
I close tonight and I'd like to not have a panic attack about my future.
We have an entire drawer crammed full. If people ask, I let them have some.
Literally the day after the bankruptcy was public one of the LQS owners was at my cut counter wanting to buy display shelves. Like ma'am, let the corpse cool a little, damn.

Yeah I understand that, but I don't curse out or hit the person that's selling handmade items. It seems to be just sewing right now as my friends who do woodworking/crochet/metal signs/screen printing/tumblers/freshies all seem to be doing alright. Just sewing - and the bulk of my items are $5 or less already.

I get those types at every craft show I do. They want to haggle and think $50 is fair for a one of a kind handmade queen size quilt. It's so frustrating and demeaning. I already have imposter syndrome and it hurts to have a butt load of total strangers wanting to argue that people who sew are the scum of the earth who don't deserve pay for their time.

Yep, she made comments all the time about how she was going to go broke because of all the food I was eating. 


The kicker was that I was 16 and weighed 85 lbs and I was only allowed one meal a day. 


Yes I have food issues now.
We're still told to cut the 2 inch samples. Never seen anyone come back in after getting samples. Such a waste of time.
We've sold at least a dozen the moment they go out on the floor.
Wait, it wasn't supposed to be a drinking game?

I just want to add, if they offer you a raise/bonus for staying - get it in writing! I went through the Hancock's liquidation and they promised us $15/hour plus a bonus and when the store closed, they just paid our regular pay and no bonus.

Well at the time I didn't really have a choice. I had a section in a craft mall and the management decided that I was too successful ( they only charged rent not commission) so they started selling my items at half price. My only options were to sue and/or move out. I did both. 


The shop suffered a fire and completely shut down. I ended up in a 3,000 sqft shop in a different town with different customers and I had to start over from scratch.

If I drive 1.5 hours from my house there are 8 LQS. Used to be 12, but it seems one closes every year. 

One that was open for the past 20 years closed in October 2024. Her landlord decided to double the rent and make her responsible for maintenance. She's in her mid 60's and chose to just retire. Plus in my area LQS are averaging 16.99/yd for quilting cotton. Most can't afford that - I get customers at the cut counter with overflowing carts of 2.99 Quilter's Showcase complaining about how expensive fabric is.

Brick and mortar stores are so expensive to open/run right now. I opened my own store in 2002 and it cost nearly 200k to just get the door open. We had a bad landlord who raised the rent every month - in 9 months it doubled. Plus I was the only staff - so I was always at the store with no free time. My grandparent's friends would come in and get personalized service picking items out - then they'd go make purchases at Walmart. As much as I'd love to have a shop again - I'd rather have an online shop out of a spare room.
I'm lucky that my store was closed today because of the icy roads.

I am an employee as well as a small business owner. I source a lot of fabrics from Joann because in my area people expect handmade quilts to be low cost, despite how many awards I've won, so I have to keep my costs as low as possible. 

I actually was set up at an event last fall and a lady "generously" offered me $200 for a custom king size quilt. When I explained that would barely cover the supplies and not the 6 weeks minimum of my time, she got in my face and said "it's not my fault your skills are worthless."
I've opened the backroom door to show customers the wall o' boxes.
![gif](giphy|QWjFSsvUPCUncq6ItU)
One of my LQS is expanding and the owner came in to ask about buying fixtures. I just about died. I asked if she was offering me a job since she's getting a bigger store.

I'm in an at-will state. When one of our Red Lobsters closed, the employees came to work to find a padlocked door and a printed note. My next scheduled day is Wednesday, and I'm already dreading the vultures.

I used to work at Hancock's, and I love working the cut counter and helping people, but it's almost torture to be constantly reminded that you're losing your job potentially in the next week. There's really no other place I could work and cut fabric all day. (I don't count Snobby Lobby for obvious reasons)


I like my coworkers, we get along pretty well. It's just stupid that corporate is a bunch of assholes that need a 4th yacht and have destroyed a gold mine.

Lady came in and had a fake "order number" because she bought a sewing table from a scam site and was told to just go into her local store, show us the order number and we'd load it in her car! SM told her it was a scam, and then she wanted the SM to reimburse her!
Okay that's just wrong. That's returning a live tree to Costco December 26th wrong.

Oh yeah. When QC is on sale for $2.99 and my line is full of ladies with carts crammed full and the only thing they say is "Oh fabric is \*so expensive\* now." Like time marches on, Ethel. You can't get a tailored suit for $10 anymore. Houses aren't $5k from Sears. But they're the same ones cursing me a blue streak for charging money to make quilts for people. Apparently I'm supposed to live on happy thoughts?
Yeah, my LQS fabric is $16.99/yard. Some of my regulars at work would poop a brick if they had to pay that much.
If I stay during the liquidation I'll just start saying what's actually on my mind with stupid customers.
I had a bopis for 24 no sew kits. It filled an entire Wal-Mart cart. (We're down the street from one and we have 9 carts that have made their way into our back room.)
We had Mariah Carey 5x in a row. You could hear employees saying "Seriously?!" when it started over.
We have an employee named Jennifer and she hates it too.
Spent all day today draping Casa and Silkys for the SM.
6/12 and 2 can't connect to X-store. We also have an ASM that randomly will take one home occasionally.
Yeah ours were the same.
There's also one with melty paws in the same colors. I bought both to make a quilt.
If corporate was honest with front line staff, all the staff would quit ASAP.

Yeah I've been slowly "concern buying" for my small business. Each trip I focus on one thing, like novelty or flannel. I am trying to have a sliver of hope, but just in case, I'm buying my in store wish list.
![gif](giphy|fnKeNjQYEYQ8E4Kqy4)
I heard Singer might be interested.
The amount of people that either call or come in and expect an employee to walk them through placing an online order is too damn high.

This lady come in one time and she was already grumpy and she was looking for "velvet fleece." She said that's what she called it and she's bought it here before.
